li_projects.title: Bicolor Matrix V2
li_projects.description: • Custom 32×8 red/green/orange LED matrix (4× HT16K33A I²C drivers) that runs as a desk clock; V2 re-routed and added chainability • Designed a 4-layer ESP32-C3 adapter board with an RTC, CO₂, temp/humidity, pressure and accelerometer sensors • Halved the adapter's length so it mounts behind the display, keeping JLCPCB cost down (~$12 PCB, ~$31 total parts)

li_projects.title: piLinkE
li_projects.description: • Compact USB-C debugger for WCH RISC-V MCUs (CH32V305, 4-layer, Altium) that also switches to ARM DAPLink mode and works as a USB-UART • DIY assembly (paste, placement, reflow) to test a low-cost assembly process • Assembled and verified by flashing/debugging a CH32 target

posts.text: I’m thrilled to share that I’ve officially earned my CompTIA SecAI+ certification! 🚀 After 2 weeks of intense preparation, I have passed with a score of 718. A huge shoutout to Mike Chapple's SecAI+ Study Guide, it was an incredibly valuable resource that provided the framework I needed to succeed. I’m looking forward to expanding my expertise in cybersecurity and applying these skills in a practical setting over the coming months. https://lnkd.in/eKPxhZpw #CompTIA #SecAIPlus

Despite getting abandoned 4 times, we still managed to win! Yesterday, I competed at UofTHacks 13 alongside Derek Yu and Evan Y.. To say it was a chaotic start would be an understatement; we had four different people join and back out of our team before and during the event. Instead of letting it slow us down, we locked in as a trio and built Wavelength. I’m proud to share that our hard work paid off: we took home the Best Use of Vultr prize! 🏆 What is Wavelength? It’s an AI recruitment platform
